priority2_architecture.why: In plain <script src> loading, the LAST script tag to define a given function name silently wins and overwrites all earlier ones. This is almost certainly why some "phase" and "reality" scripts appear to have no effect — an older script loaded after them redefines the same function back to its fake behaviour.
priority2_architecture.safe_fix: Check script tag order at the bottom of index.html. Whichever file is listed last for a duplicated function name is the one actually running. Delete or rename the losing definitions rather than trying to patch a function that never executes.

priority3_optimization.problem: Large number of index*.html.backup_* / index_before_*.html files in the repo root
priority3_optimization.why: Not a runtime risk (nothing loads them), but they make it hard to know which file is authoritative and bloat the repo.
priority3_optimization.safe_fix: Move to an archive/ folder or delete once you confirm current index.html is stable. Never edit a backup file expecting it to affect the live app.

priority3_optimization.problem: Very high number of one-off "install"/"phase"/"reality" scripts, most of which are not referenced by any <script src> in index.html and were likely one-time Node scripts run once to patch files, not part of the running app.
priority3_optimization.why: These add no risk if unreferenced, but make the codebase very hard to reason about and hide which changes actually took effect.
priority3_optimization.safe_fix: For each one, check if it is a build-time patch script (fine to archive after running) or something the browser is expected to load (must appear in a <script src>). If neither, archive it.
